title: PR drafting resolves base scope and treats validation evidence conservatively

provenance.originSummary: Synthetic benchmark matrix for pull request identity, comparison-base, preflight, and validation-evidence behavior.
provenance.whyItMattered: A draft can be materially wrong if pull request authority is assigned by similarity, existing pull request scope hides local changes, or skipped and stale tests are reported as passing.
provenance.genericCondition: Sanitized runs combine active and historical pull request trust states, local and remote commit relations, conditional base policy, local unpushed changes, service-scope conflict, and multiple validation evidence states.

description: A matrix covering identity-aware pull request authority, local commit relations, active pull request base metadata plus local changes, conditional policy failure, unrelated service hard stop, and conservative validation evidence.

scope.notes: The fixture defines independent runs for base, preflight, scope-conflict, and validation-evidence decisions.

mustCatch.description: Active repository-and-branch identity, exact final-head identity, and commit association receive distinct trust levels; title or path similarity never promotes authority.
An active identity records equal, ahead, behind, diverged, or unknown local relation while retaining all committed and working-tree evidence; behind, diverged, and unknown remain visible gaps.
Existing pull request base metadata selects the base but does not replace committed, staged, unstaged, or untracked local evidence.
The selected base commit supplies the pull request template and contributor policy while the common ancestor is used only as the diff origin.

The template, opening guide, and changelog guide always load from the selected base, while new-resource, Resource Identity, and List Resource guides load only when classified paths make them applicable.
A missing applicable template or contributor guide at the selected base produces the exact named-source hard stop.
Unrelated primary changes in two service packages stop drafting before a title is guessed.
Only successful current-run applicable validation is reported as passing; skipped, missing, stale, and contradicted evidence remain unchecked and visible as gaps.
The workflow fingerprints HEAD, staged and unstaged tracked content, and untracked names and bytes; one mismatch discards all evidence and restarts, while a second mismatch hard-stops.
Remote base refresh uses an explicit source-to-remote-tracking refspec with no-tags, no-recurse-submodules, and no-write-fetch-head.

Fingerprint collection invokes the checked-in standard-library Go helper instead of generated PowerShell, Bash, or inline code, supports direct Go on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and uses the same execution environment for both fingerprints.

When native Windows cannot provide one suitable worktree with Git and Go, the workflow can inspect an explicitly selected WSL distribution, prefer a validated WSL-native checkout, or invoke the helper against the same mounted worktree through argument-safe translation.
Every terminal batch shows its exact command under Read-only or the one full remote-tracking-ref update label, and fetch is never mixed with inspection commands.

The helper resolves Git's absolute top-level worktree with git rev-parse --show-toplevel and uses it for all commands and untracked-path joins, so an interior repository-root argument cannot omit or misjoin root-level evidence.
The Windows fallback passes the repository path separately to wslpath and the translated path separately to wsl.exe --cd, preserving spaces without interpolating either path into Bash code.
A suitable current worktree with Git and Go is selected directly on native, WSL, container, Codespaces, SSH, and remote terminals without invoking a host-specific fallback.
Repository discovery runs only after current-worktree validation fails and searches disclosed developer-configured roots plus existing conventional roots without scanning the whole filesystem.

Every candidate is validated by canonical Git root, repository structure and remotes, expected checked-out branch, full HEAD, dirty state, and Git and Go capability rather than directory or branch name alone.
A clean clone with the same branch and HEAD is not substituted for a known source checkout with staged, unstaged, or untracked changes.
Multiple trustworthy candidates produce a developer selection request containing environment, canonical path, branch, full HEAD, and dirty-state summaries rather than an automatic path-order choice.
When no candidate satisfies identity, branch, state, and capability checks, the workflow requests an explicit repository path and names the missing checks instead of guessing.

Native Windows uses native Git and Go when suitable; optional WSL fallback verifies an explicitly selected distribution and searches bounded roots for a WSL-native checkout before offering argument-safe translation of the same Windows worktree.
Repository inspection, fingerprints, pull request evidence, base resolution, diff collection, and payload generation reuse one recorded canonical worktree and execution environment.

mustNotFlag.description: Existing pull request text must not erase local unpushed changes from scope.
Exact final-head or commit-association-only prior pull request metadata must not choose the current comparison base or override current base-revision policy.
Unspecified scope-equivalence or title similarity must remain advisory rather than becoming authoritative pull request evidence.
A successful process exit with skipped acceptance tests must not check the local-test item without required environment evidence.
Unchanged HEAD must not be treated as stable when staged, unstaged, or untracked evidence changed during the run.
A targeted remote base refresh must not omit no-write-fetch-head or use an implicit destination ref.
A missing Go result from one non-interactive WSL shell must not be treated as proof that the selected distribution lacks Go.
The workflow must not generate a PowerShell or Bash fingerprint implementation at runtime.
A command that updates remote-tracking metadata must not run under a Read-only label or without naming its one destination ref.
The workflow must not compare an initial fingerprint produced by one Git executable or environment with a final fingerprint produced by another.
The helper must not join Git root-relative untracked paths to an interior directory supplied by the caller.
Windows or WSL repository paths must not be spliced into one shell command string where spaces or shell characters can change argument boundaries.
A slow but progressing Git index refresh under /mnt/c must not be treated as a portability failure or terminated solely because Windows-to-WSL filesystem synchronization is slow.
A Windows host must not trigger WSL when native Git and Go can use the suitable current worktree.
A matching directory name or branch name alone must not make a repository candidate trustworthy.
Branch and HEAD equality must not erase staged, unstaged, or untracked differences between checkouts.
Repository discovery must not recursively scan filesystem roots, arbitrary drives, or all mounted volumes.
The workflow must not inspect one checkout, fingerprint another, or generate the payload from a different execution environment.

mustIncludeMarkers: Cannot run draft-pr-description: required base-revision source is missing:
Cannot run draft-pr-description: unrelated primary changes span multiple service packages.
Cannot run draft-pr-description: repository state changed repeatedly during evidence collection.
No observed current-run local test evidence.
mustNotIncludeMarkers: Tests passed locally based on the existing pull request body.

notes: Each scenario is a separate prompt invocation; hard-stop scenarios intentionally do not emit the normal five-section output. Scope-equivalent prior pull request promotion is intentionally deferred.
